what_happened: Retry A3 of the in-flight table job (the table records the live work tree and the checks stage) was rejected at the final verdict. There was one major finding. No acceptance criteria are listed as unmet and no checks as failed. The real drain finds the checks stage by matching a UI display string in StageWatch::line (drain.rs ~1876). When the producer is sent back after a failed check, the display string still says checks, so the table says "checks" while the producer is running again. A restarted drain would then read the wrong stage.
cause: The stage the table records is derived from presentation text rather than from the pipeline's own state. Nothing requires stage changes to come from a typed source, and nothing exercises the loop-back path (producer sent back after checks) against the real drain. Tests that pass a stage value directly or follow only the forward path cannot show the mismatch. This is the same retry of the same job: the previous attempt (earlier case 20261030-004950-fqve) was also rejected on the in-flight table's real-drain accuracy. Only the verifier reading the diff at the final verdict compares what the table records with the real stage, and there rejection is the only outcome. This is an inference, since the stored fields do not show the plan or tests.
prevention: Have the producer and checks code emit typed stage events (an enum with Producer, Checks and so on) at each transition, including the send-back transition, and have the in-flight table record only those. Do not parse display strings. Add a test that runs the real drain path through checks failing and the producer being sent back. It must assert that the recorded stage returns to the producer stage and that the recorded work tree is the producer's live one. Add a check that fails if the table writer reads text meant for display.
proposed_request: Retry the in-flight table job (earlier attempts 20261029-142853-x4nr and 20261030-005008-tf2s). Outcome: the in-flight table always shows the stage a running job is really in and its live producer work tree, including after checks fail and the producer is sent back. Acceptance: (1) The table's stage comes from a typed stage value set where the pipeline changes stage (crates/athena-core/src/run/producer.rs and the drain), not from matching the display line in StageWatch::line. (2) When the producer is sent back after a failed check, the table shows the producer stage again, not checks. (3) The recorded work tree is the producer's live work tree, not the kept-work directory. (4) A test drives the real drain and stage code through producer, checks, send-back, producer, checks, and asserts the recorded stage and work tree at each step. A restarted drain reads the table correctly. Keep the existing changes: write the table at stage changes and read it when the drain starts. Production files in drain.rs and run/producer.rs may change, with tests.
